messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Burns <claire@aerohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot Acceptance Canvas + MAP Slide Skeleton — initial co-edit

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I put together a lightweight MAP (mutual action plan) seed and a one‑slide executive skeleton to help align the pilot acceptance criteria and the close timeline. The goal: a compact checklist we can use to unblock procurement and start a 45‑day pilot.

Quick summary (in the attached MAP canvas and slides):
- Week 0: access + test dataset upload (security & onboarding)
- Week 1–2: technical validation (throughput, latency, KV cache behavior)
- Week 3: feature validation (edge cases, hallucination checks, eval prompts)
- Week 4–6: pilot run, capture metrics + success signals
- Acceptance: business signoff + SLOs met on latency/accuracy + security checklist completed

Asks:
1) Can you grant edit access to the AeroHealth PMO so they can add acceptance stakeholders?
2) Review the acceptance criteria on the GDoc and flag any "must have" items you want moved to Week 1.
3) If the timeline looks tight, we can expand to a 60‑day pilot — ping me with constraints.

Attachments: pilot-map-canvas.xlsx (MAP canvas), map-slide-skeleton.pptx (exec slide skeleton).
GDoc/GSlide links are below for co‑editing.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short kickoff invite once we have edit access set.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot Acceptance Canvas + MAP Slide Skeleton — initial co-edit

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the draft. Quick notes:

- Overall this looks great. Two immediate asks from my side: please add an explicit security checkpoint for data retention policy signoff (we need to confirm retention + deletion for PHI) and add an SLA latency threshold (p50 < 200ms on typical queries) as an acceptance metric.
- Our procurement team will want sample contract language around data residency; I CC'd PMO to start that thread.
- 45 days seems doable, but can you call out a 7‑day buffer at the end for acceptance signoff?

Would love to co‑edit the slide with a short blurb for our exec sponsor. I’ll add my comments in the GDoc now.

— Claire
Claire Burns
Director of Product, AeroHealth
claire@aerohealth.com

Adding a few technical validation checkpoints to the MAP (I’ve pasted them below and also uploaded a short checklist):

Technical validation (proposed Week 1–2):
- Baseline throughput at expected QPS (test harness + sample dataset)
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) with target p50 < 200ms, p95 < 750ms
- KV cache correctness: validate cold vs warm KV responses on long‑context flows
- Memory/CPU usage on Dedicated nodes during burst windows
- End‑to‑end telemetry route checks (trace IDs, sample logs)

I attached tech‑validation checklist (tech-validation-checklist.md) and made inline comments in the GDoc where I recommend moving a few acceptance items earlier (security retention + SLA items).

I also added a short paragraph in the slide notes calling out the guardrail: "If any acceptance SLO (latency or security) is unmet after the buffer window, we’ll run a targeted remediation sprint and extend the pilot by 14 days."

Happy to jump on a short call next week to walk through the test harness.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
